purpose: Repaint the older Hindu films reused in wave 1 (month one) so no two look the same (owner: "We can't have the same look for every film... You don't go to AMC and watch a movie that looks like the last one").
rules: no two Hindu month-one films within 3 days of each other share a look (new or reused); neighbouring days never match
each shot keeps its story beat and framing from the existing art; only the look changes (the old still is uploaded to ChatGPT as the layout reference)
no text in images unless the look needs it; vertical 9:16; no rainbow gradients
today shots get a diverse modern cast
deities only in respectful traditional iconography; no mockery
keep the beheading of the boy off-screen (a flash of light), no harm shown
neighbours: new month-one Hindu films: 1 neon, 2 anime, 3 miniature, 4 comic, 5 impasto, 6 cutout, 8 inkwash, 9 film35, 11 woodblock, 12 riso, 14 inkwash, 15 popcinema, 17 kalighat, 18 chrome, 19 mural, 20 vhs, 21 impasto, 22 clay, 23 kalighat, 27 cutout, 28 film35, 29 anime, 30 mural.

films.suffix: 1960s pop-art print, big Ben-Day dots, thick black outlines, flat punchy red, yellow, cyan and hot pink, graphic close-up framing, maximal contrast
films.why: a forest robber turned poet: loud pop-art punch

shots.name: VA1-Forest-Robber
shots.beat: As tradition tells it, a robber named Ratnakara lived in the forest. He stopped travelers and took everything they had, to feed his family.

shots.name: VA2-Narada
shots.beat: One day he stopped a wandering sage, Narada, who asked him one quiet question: “Will your family share the weight of what you’re doing?”

shots.name: VA3-The-Answer
shots.beat: Ratnakara ran home and asked. And they said no. “You chose this. It’s yours.”

shots.name: VA4-A-Name
shots.beat: He came back shaken. Narada gave him a name of God to repeat, and Ratnakara sat down to repeat it.

shots.name: VA5-Anthill
shots.beat: He sat so still, for so long, that ants built a hill over him.

shots.name: VA6-Valmiki
shots.beat: When he rose, people called him Valmiki, “the one from the anthill.” And Valmiki went on to write the Ramayana.

films.suffix: Kalighat pat painting, sweeping confident brush outlines, flat watercolour fills, bold curves, Bengali folk flair, bold saturated colour, big sweeping black brush lines
films.why: a picture about the soul changing clothes: bold Kalighat lines (redone; the editorial try stayed too close to the old art)
films.todayCast: a Guyanese-American Hindu woman in her forties in Queens

shots.name: NC1-A-Picture
shots.beat: In the Gita, Krishna gives Arjuna a simple picture.

shots.name: NC2-Old-Clothes
shots.beat: Just as a person sets aside worn-out clothes, and puts on new ones,

shots.name: NC3-New-Clothes
shots.beat: so the soul leaves a worn-out body behind, and takes on a new one.

shots.name: NC4-Atman
shots.beat: In Hindu thought, the real you, the atman, is never worn out, never damaged, never old.

shots.name: NC5-Changes-Clothes
shots.beat: It just changes clothes.

shots.name: NC6-Today
shots.beat: The real you isn’t worn out. Only the clothes are.
shots.cast: a Guyanese-American Hindu woman in her forties in Queens

films.suffix: claymation-look stop-motion set, handmade plasticine figures with visible fingerprints, miniature practical props, soft studio light, shallow depth of field, bright saturated plasticine colours, playful
films.why: a sage who wanders heaven and earth with his veena: playful claymation (redone; anime stayed too close)
films.todayCast: a young Tamil-Malaysian man on a Kuala Lumpur train

shots.name: ND1-Wanderer
shots.beat: Narada is the wandering sage of Hindu stories. He shows up everywhere: in heaven, on earth, in every kingdom.

shots.name: ND2-Narada
shots.beat: He usually carries his veena, a stringed instrument.

shots.name: ND3-Two-Words
shots.beat: And everywhere he goes, he says the same two words: Narayana, Narayana. A name of Vishnu.

shots.name: ND4-Everywhere
shots.beat: He says it walking. He says it arriving. He says it leaving.

shots.name: ND5-Part-Of-Him
shots.beat: It’s so much part of him that in Indian movies and cartoons, you know Narada has arrived when you hear it.

shots.name: ND6-Today
shots.beat: A tiny habit, repeated so often it became who he is. Hindus call it japa.
shots.cast: a young Tamil-Malaysian man on a Kuala Lumpur train

films.suffix: Gond tribal painting from central India, figures and animals filled with fine dot-and-dash line patterns, bold flat colours on a dark ground, hot orange, turquoise, lime and magenta, joyful and graphic
films.why: animals building a bridge: Gond tribal art is made for creatures

shots.name: SQ1-The-Bridge
shots.beat: Rama’s army was building a bridge of stones across the ocean. Giant monkeys and bears hauled huge boulders.

shots.name: SQ2-The-Squirrel
shots.beat: And a little squirrel wanted to help too.

shots.name: SQ3-Sand
shots.beat: It rolled in the sand, ran onto the bridge, and shook the sand off between the stones. Again, and again.

shots.name: SQ4-They-Laugh
shots.beat: The monkeys laughed.

shots.name: SQ5-Rama
shots.beat: Rama didn’t. He picked the squirrel up and gently stroked its back. And that, the story says, is why Indian squirrels have three stripes.

shots.name: SQ6-Today
shots.beat: Small efforts count. Two minutes a day, again and again, adds up.

films.suffix: single comic-book panel, bold inks, halftone shading, dynamic camera angles, strong flat colour, no speech bubbles, no lettering, graphic-novel inks, deep blacks, one hot accent colour
films.why: a guard at the door, a clash, a new life: graphic-novel drama (no harm shown)

shots.name: GH1-Turmeric
shots.beat: Parvati made a boy from turmeric paste, and breathed life into him.

shots.name: GH2-At-The-Door
shots.beat: Guard my door, she said, and let no one in.

shots.name: GH3-Shiva-Returns
shots.beat: Then Shiva came home. Neither knew who the other was, and there was a terrible misunderstanding at the door.

shots.name: GH4-Grief
shots.beat: Parvati’s grief shook the whole universe. Shiva, heartbroken, set out to make it right.

shots.name: GH5-New-Life
shots.beat: His followers came back with an elephant’s head. Shiva gave the boy new life, and a promise: from now on, you will be honored first.

shots.name: GH6-Today
shots.beat: Something broken can become something new, and even better.

films.suffix: Madhubani (Mithila) folk painting, bold double black outlines, every surface filled with fish-scale, leaf and line patterns, vivid vermilion, turmeric yellow, leaf green and indigo, flat decorative space
films.why: a family race around the world: Madhubani folk painting from Mithila
films.todayCast: a Mauritian Hindu family: mother, father and young daughter

shots.name: GF1-Kailash
shots.beat: On Mount Kailash, Shiva and Parvati held up one perfect fruit for their two sons, Ganesha and Kartikeya.

shots.name: GF2-The-Race
shots.beat: “Whoever goes around the whole world first,” they said, “wins it.”

shots.name: GF3-Peacock
shots.beat: Kartikeya leapt onto his peacock and shot off across the sky.

shots.name: GF4-Three-Times
shots.beat: Ganesha looked at his ride, a tiny mouse. Then he stood, and slowly walked around his parents, three times.

shots.name: GF5-Whole-World
shots.beat: “You two are my whole world,” he said. “I’ve been around it.” His parents laughed, and gave him the fruit.

shots.name: GF6-Today
shots.beat: And so, before weddings, new homes and first days, Hindus begin with Ganesha.
shots.cast: a Mauritian Hindu family: mother, father and young daughter

films.suffix: two- or three-colour risograph poster print, bold flat shapes, slightly misregistered ink, halftone dots, lime and black with one accent colour, lime, black and hot pink, big flat shapes, punchy
films.why: a sage dictating, a god writing through the night: punchy risograph poster

shots.name: K01-Himalaya
shots.beat: Long ago, the sage Vyasa carried a whole epic in his mind: the Mahabharata, one of the longest poems ever composed.

shots.name: K02-The-Request
shots.beat: He needed someone to write it down as he spoke. So he asked Ganesha.

shots.name: K03-One-Condition
shots.beat: Ganesha agreed, on one condition: once Vyasa began, he must not stop.

shots.name: K04-Do-You-Understand
shots.beat: Vyasa added a condition of his own: Ganesha must understand every verse before writing it.

shots.name: K05-Night-Work
shots.beat: So it began, day and night. Whenever Vyasa needed time to think, he recited a hard verse, and Ganesha paused to understand it.

shots.name: K06-The-Pen-Breaks
shots.beat: In one popular telling, in the middle of it all, the pen breaks.

shots.name: K07-The-Tusk-Writes
shots.beat: Ganesha broke off a piece of his own tusk, and kept writing.

shots.name: K08-Sunrise
shots.beat: Verse by verse, the great story was written down, and understood.

shots.name: K09-Today
shots.beat: That’s why so many images of Ganesha show one broken tusk, often with the broken piece in his hand.
